Sure! If you’re looking to check the **current time** from the Command Prompt on Windows, there’s a quick way:

```batch
C:\>echo %TIME%
```

This will display something like:
```
14:32:07.45
```

If you prefer to capture this value into a variable or write it to a text file, you could use:

```batch
@echo off
set CURRENT_TIME=%TIME%
echo Current Time: %CURRENT_TIME% > C:\temp\clock.txt
```

That writes the timestamp (e.g., “14:32:07.45”) into `C:\temp\clock.txt`.
